newsitem.title: USA: Swiss Nat'l Bank economist sees no recovery signs.
newsitem.headline: Swiss Nat'l Bank economist sees no recovery signs.

text.p: Swiss National Bank chief economist Georg Rich on Thursday said he had seen no evidence that Switzerland's economy had started to recover and that the central bank would only raise interest rates after "clear signs" that a recovery was under way.
"We haven't seen any evidence that an economic recovery has started," Rich told Reuters after delivering a speech at the Graduate School and University Center of the City University of New York.
"As long as we have no firm proof, I don't see how we could adjust economic policy," he added.
Rich said the Swiss National Bank was looking to output and employment measures to provide the first sign of an economic recovery.

"Of course, we would look at the usual measures of output, real GDP (gross domestic product), as it grows to its potential level. We will certainly look at labor markets, in addition, to see signs of labor market tightness," Rich said.

When asked about the possibility of preemptive rate increases to ward off any inflationary pressures, Rich said: "If we are really concerned about price stability, we should possibly tighten early in the recovery."
Rich said Switzerland must go through a "painful period of structural adjustment" to make industries there more efficient and competitive.
